title: Microphase release conductor: slate, observability notes, and quick rollback
summary: Working notes and compact checklist for a microphase (small-cohort) rollout of the model-routing update + deployment of the request-batching tweak. Includes an hourly watchlist, signal thresholds, smoke test scripts, and a skeletal release notes draft for product comms.
objectives: Deploy model-routing v2.3 with updated fallback policy (region-first then cost-tier) to 5% of traffic for 4 hours
Roll out continuous batching tweak to serving runtime on canary pool to reduce p99 token latency by ~7%
Validate telemetry and automatic fallback paths; ensure no regression to customer-facing latency SLOs
Produce short release note for product and customer success summarizing change and known caveats
preflight-checklist: Merge approval: runtime PR #2187 has 2 approvals and green CI
Integration smoke: local end-to-end test run passing (e2e-smoke-v2)
Canary pool health: baseline CPU/GPU utilization and KV-cache hit rates recorded at t-24h
Config pin: model-routing config saved as routing/v2.3 pinned for canary tenants
Backout artifacts prepared: previous model-routing config and runtime image tagged: runtime:v2.2-rollback-ready
Pager and on-call: release engineer and SRE on-call assigned; Slack channel #release-microphase created and pinned
Data retention and logs: KMS keys available and logs archiving confirmed for 30d
hourly-watchlist: T-minus 60: final confirmation, notify stakeholders (CS, infra, SRE, runtime). Snapshot dashboards and save links.
T-minus 30: start 5% traffic ramp to canary. Post ramp note in channel with sample request ids.
T+15m: validate basic success rate (>99.5% HTTP 2xx for gen/chat endpoints). Check error spikes.
T+45m: check latency buckets: p50/p90/p99 compared to baseline. p99 must not increase >10% over baseline.
T+2h: inspect KV-cache hit ratio and batching efficiency metrics. Expect KV hit within +-3% of baseline.
T+4h: if stable, keep at 5% for additional 2h and prepare gradual ramp to 20% only after ops signoff.
Immediate anomalies: apply traffic-evacuation (see rollback plan) if invocation error >1% or sustained p99 latency >25% above baseline for 10 minutes
signal-thresholds: Error rate (5xx + runtime exceptions): abort if >1% sustained over 5m
User-facing latency (p99): abort if >25% above baseline for 10m
Token generation failures (incoherent outputs / truncated sequences): abort and capture 100 sample traces
KV cache miss spike: investigate if miss rate increases >10% relative to baseline
CPU/GPU OOM or throttling: immediate abort and escalate to infra on-call
smoke-tests: run_smoke_prompt_suite.sh --canary - collects 200 samples across chat and streaming endpoints
validate_embedding_pipeline.py --end-to-end - checks embedding consistency for seeded dataset (allowed drift <0.5%)
trace_sample_and_shelve: capture 50 low-latency and 50 high-latency traces to S3 bucket s3://redwood-release-microphase/2026-03-12/
oss-compat-run: invoke third-party adapter to ensure model-variant fallback still resolves within 150ms
rollback_plan: Traffic evac -> immediate rollback to routing/v2.2 and runtime:v2.2-rollback-ready images. Steps: 1) Flip canary traffic weight to 0% via traffic-router API; 2) Revert model-routing config (routing/v2.2); 3) Restart canary instances with runtime:v2.2-rollback-ready if necessary; 4) Run verification smoke tests; 5) Notify stakeholders and open postmortem ticket if rollback occurred. Time objective: <10 minutes to zero traffic from detection to evacuation for on-prem regions, <6 minutes for hosted API regions.
post-deploy-validation: Confirm fix: run smoke-tests and get green for >=30m after rollback or 2h after stable deployment
Telemetry capture: ensure full trace export for all flagged anomalies; attach sample ids to JIRA ticket
Customer-impact check: sample CS cases in top 3 tenants in canary cohort to ensure no visible regressions
Stability window: recommend 72h high-signal monitoring with daily handoff notes
communications: Pre-deploy: 30m heads-up to #release-microphase with docket and watchlist
On deploy: minute-by-minute check-ins in channel, automated dashboard snapshots every 15m
If rollback: short note to #release-ops and product with one-line summary and link to incident ticket
Post-deploy: 1-page release note for CS + short changelog for product docs (see release_notes_draft field)
release_notes_draft:
Short changelog (for CS / product):
- model-routing: v2.3 (canary 5%): introduces locality-first fallback ordering to reduce cross-region latency and better align with cost tiers. Expected impact: small reduction in average latency for geo-local traffic; may change routing behavior for multi-region tenants.
- runtime batching tweak: continuous batching kernel adjustment to improve p99 token latency by ~7% in typical workloads.
Known caveats: there is a ~5% chance of increased cache churn on cold clusters; we will monitor KV-cache hit ratios closely. If customers observe unexpected behaviour, please collect request ids and traces and escalate to release channel.
Contact: cs@redwood.ai (internal: @Priya Shah, @Daniel Kim)
followups_and_open_questions: Should we extend the canary to 48h for enterprise tenants that have pinned models? pros/cons to discuss with product
Is the autoscaling cooldown acceptable for dedicated pools during the burst window? Marcus to confirm with infra
Need a post-release eval harness to compare output-text-quality vs v2.2 on a seeded prompt set. Research to own (Priya)
